# In Crocoddyl whole-body manipulation, is the friction cone and CoP/ZMP cost sufficient? When should a contact wrench cone be used?

> **Current answer:** The maintainer explicitly states that a single friction constraint is insufficient, a single CoP (center of pressure) constraint is also insufficient, and a contact wrench cone is required. The original author interpreted the wrench cone as encompassing friction, ZMP/CoP boundaries, and yaw torque boundaries, and the maintainer confirms this is correct. When using a wrench cone, the individual friction cone or CoP cost should be removed; the old example did not integrate it because it was written before the feature was available.

## Key terms

- Contact wrench cone (接触力矩锥)
- Friction cone (摩擦锥)
- Center of pressure (CoP) (压力中心)
- Yaw torque (偏航力矩)

## Problem and symptoms

- Is a friction cone or CoP/ZMP cost sufficient in whole-body manipulation? When should a contact wrench cone be used?
- How should the wrench cone be oriented when the feet are not aligned with the world frame?
- Users cannot determine the relationship between friction cones, CoP/ZMP costs, and contact wrench cones in high dynamic whole-body operations.
- When the foot has a yaw angle, users are unclear on how the wrench cone rotation matrix is defined.

## Environment

- Crocoddyl whole_body_manipulation example, thread time from 2020-10 to 2021-02; no Crocoddyl version or robot model provided.

## Priority diagnostics

- Contact models require separate checks for tangential friction, CoP support domain, and yaw torque boundaries, rather than just seeing a friction cone and assuming full stability.
- The wrench cone constructor's first rotation parameter should be verified against the actual foot orientation.

## Possible causes

- The example was written before the contact wrench cone functionality was developed; the maintainer explains this is the reason for the example still using a friction cone, not indicating that it is sufficient.

## Attempts

- The author reviewed the contact wrench cone paper and confirmed with the maintainer whether it covers friction, ZMP/CoP, and yaw torque boundaries.
- The author provided images of feet not aligned with the world coordinate system and asked for the rotation matrix.

## Effective fixes

- Use the contact wrench cone when the full finite foot constraint is required, and remove individual friction cones or CoP costs to avoid duplication.
- When feet are not aligned with the world frame, specify the rotation using the constructor of the wrench cone.

## Result

- The author clarified the issue and stated they will update the example after the scheme is worked out; no subsequent implementation or numerical results are provided.
- The rotation parameter issue is only mentioned by the maintainer in the interface, without author verification.

## Safety notes

- In high dynamic real-world operations, monitor friction margin, CoP support domain, and yaw torque; an incorrect constraint reference system may result in seemingly feasible but non-executable contact forces.
